payload.reason: The evidence provides specific performance metrics and comparisons for multilingual BERT (M-Bert) in various settings, indicating its effectiveness relative to baselines.

claims.text: M-Bert performs better than majority class baselines in cross-lingual and cross-target settings, although it performs worse in cross-target than in cross-lingual settings.
M-Bert has established itself as state of the art for various multilingual tasks, outperforming feature-based and other neural approaches in monolingual English settings.
Cross-lingual performance of M-Bert improves when questions are presented in English, indicating a benefit from using a lingua franca during evaluation.
